name: SM_Fireplace_Fieldstone_PR
supersedes: Stonebrook/SM_Fireplace_Fieldstone_01 (4.02 x 1.54 x 4.145 m, base_center) and its FiredClay / V2 refinements
dresses: fieldstone cottage hearth, 4.0 x 1.54 x 4.14 m: rubble jambs with dressed stones up the opening and corners, an oak bressummer and mantel shelf over a 1.6 x 1.5 m opening, a smoke-blackened fireback and breast, a stack in a second stage with weathered shoulders, a flagged hearth, two iron fire dogs carrying three logs burnt through in the middle on a bed of ash, a swinging crane with a pot hook

fit.pivot: base centre of the 4.0 x 1.54 m footprint; opening faces -Y, the back (+Y) stands against the wall

emissive.type: hearth fire (no flame mesh in the FBX: use the engine fire, sprite seq hearth_fire, on the logs)
emissive.note: point light among the logs with a 15 cm soft source radius, flicker 10-20 percent at 4-9 Hz; a second dim red light (1200 K, 2 m radius) on the ash bed sells the embers; the logs carry no emissive ember mask

material_exception: shared tiling scan sets with a vertex-colour weathering layer (MI_Prop_* / MI_Struct_*), not private bakes and not yet rows of ART_STANDARD.md section 2. Edge wear, stains and soot are per-vertex. A unique bake per prop is the next step where the weaknesses say so.
known_weaknesses: Masonry reads as real rubble with dressed jamb stones; soot on fireback and breast is the vertex-colour soot switch on a coarse grid, so its edge is soft; logs are swept tubes with a charred middle, no bark, no split faces, no embers; the bressummer has no adze marks; stack top is cut square at 4.14 m as the mesh it replaces. Brick version of sprite 64 frame 5 not built.
